ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Nelson Mandela Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: First visit after a biopsy diagnosis of localized prostate cancer: risk group, staging, baseline before treatment, and radiation oncology referral. Concerns: Wants to understand a new diagnosis of prostate cancer after a rising PSA, and what treatment would mean at his age and with his commitments; Wants to keep his travel and public work going during treatment. [S]

tr.td: Bicalutamide 50 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily for four weeks, to block the testosterone flare at the start of leuprolide
One tablet once daily for four weeks

Leuprolide acetate 22.5 mg injection (three-month depot), intramuscular, two doses twelve weeks apart (the second given at a primary care visit), about six months of androgen deprivation with radiotherapy
One injection every twelve weeks, two doses
Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3) 1000 units oral tablet, one tablet by mouth once daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg oral capsule, one capsule by mouth once daily after the evening meal, for urinary frequency during radiotherapy
One capsule once daily in the evening

Multiparametric MRI of the prostate: gland volume 28 mL with a resection defect from the earlier operation; 9 mm PI-RADS 4 lesion in the left peripheral zone at the mid-gland; no extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or enlarged pelvic nodes

MRI-ultrasound fusion transperineal biopsy of the prostate, at the urology practice: adenocarcinoma, Gleason 4+3 (Grade Group 3) in 1 of 2 targeted cores (30 percent of the core) and in 2 of 12 systematic cores (Gleason 3+4, 10 and 15 percent); 3 of 14 cores in all; no perineural invasion
Gallium-68 PSMA PET/CT for staging: uptake only in the left peripheral zone of the prostate; no nodal, bone, or visceral disease (N0 M0)
Transperineal insertion of three gold fiducial markers into the prostate for image guidance, with planning CT and MRI

Image-guided intensity-modulated radiotherapy to the prostate and proximal seminal vesicles, 74 Gy in 37 daily fractions over about seven and a half weeks, with curative intent; no pelvic nodal radiation
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes

tr.td: First visit after a biopsy diagnosis of localized prostate cancer: risk group, staging, baseline before treatment, and radiation oncology referral
Five-week follow-up with radiation oncology consultation: staging result, shared decision on treatment, start of androgen deprivation, and bone density
Three-month follow-up on androgen deprivation before radiotherapy: PSA, testosterone, vitamin D, and side effects
Follow-up six weeks after radiotherapy: PSA, urinary and bowel effects, end of androgen deprivation, and the surveillance plan
Radiation oncology consultation to review staging and discuss curative treatment options and short-term androgen deprivation
Staging for unfavorable intermediate-risk disease with PSMA PET/CT

Treatment chosen through shared decision-making: image-guided external beam radiotherapy to the prostate with six months of androgen deprivation (leuprolide, with bicalutamide for the first four weeks)
Androgen deprivation monitoring: testosterone, PSA, blood pressure, glucose and lipids, DXA at baseline and every one to two years, vitamin D and calcium, hot flashes, mood, and cognition
After radiotherapy: PSA every six months for five years, then yearly, with recurrence defined as a rise of 2 ng/mL above the nadir (Phoenix); urinary and bowel symptoms at every visit
Distress screening at each visit, physical activity, and a written survivorship care plan
Reach an informed, shared decision on treatment after hearing every reasonable option, including observation
Radiotherapy with six months of androgen deprivation chosen at the radiation oncology consultation
Complete six months of androgen deprivation and the course of radiotherapy with side effects managed
Two leuprolide depots and 37 fractions completed; testosterone castrate on treatment; mild hot flashes and urinary frequency, managed
Protect bone health on androgen deprivation: baseline DXA, vitamin D of 30 ng/mL or more, dietary calcium, and weight-bearing exercise
Femoral neck T-score -1.4; vitamin D 34 ng/mL on supplementation; walking daily
PSA falling after radiotherapy, with a written surveillance plan
PSA 0.4 ng/mL six weeks after radiotherapy; PSA every six months planned
